sourceRefs.locator: pp. 220–223, figs. 1–2 and n. 4. Two neighbouring sites and more than 1,300 graves used from the final third of the fifth century to the end of the seventh.
Project description, cemetery plan and photograph caption for grave 90. A disc brooch and beads from a necklace at chest level, first half of the seventh century.
Opening paragraphs and excavation plan. Settlement traces, sixth to eleventh centuries, 200 metres downslope from the cemetery. Both surface buildings and sunken buildings are documented.
pp. 20–21, figs. 1, 3–5. Seventh-century evidence and several superimposed dwellings, longhouses interpreted as byre-dwellings, clay loom weights from sunken buildings.
pp. 222–224, 231, figs. 3–4. Successive houses, few datable finds from postholes, sixth-century material and the long life of the settlement.
pp. 296–297, discussion of the genitium, screona and sunken buildings. Textile tools frequently occur in secondary fills. Single-purpose and gendered interpretations require further evidence.

pp. 179–181, opening counts and fig. 1. 22,155 beads in the cemetery; individual groups range from a few beads to more than 300. Section on Mosaikperlen and Millefioriperlen explains cross-cut patterned glass canes.
pp. 298–302, figs. 4a–c. Reconstructed successive fence lines in the south-eastern sector. Phase II encloses four graves, including graves 24 and 25 dated to the last third of the seventh century.

Publisher’s description, paragraphs beginning “In direkter Nachbarschaft” and “200 Meter entfernt”. The completed catalogue records 86 burials in small cemeteries adjoining six farmsteads around AD 700.
pp. 227–231, figs. 5, 6 and 9, n. 12. Waterlogged graves at the eastern farm, winter 703/704 felling date for freshly worked oak of grave 27, and the excavator’s dating of the burial to early 704.

Object data and Beschreibung, inventory 1989-0011-0769-9000. Mortised bed, wooden dowels and wedge, single bottom board, red and black decoration, leather and plant fibres, and gables added for the burial.

labels.de: Spätes 5. Jh. · Ein Friedhof am Hang
labels.en: Late 5th century · A burial ground on the slope

summary.de: 485 steht hier für das letzte Drittel des fünften Jahrhunderts, in das die frühesten Gräber datieren.
summary.en: 485 represents the final third of the fifth century, the archaeological date of the earliest graves.

summary.de: 550 ist ein Lesejahr für die Siedlungsspuren des sechsten Jahrhunderts. Die einzelnen Neubauten haben unterschiedliche und meist viel gröbere Datierungen.
summary.en: 550 is a viewing year for the sixth-century settlement evidence. Individual rebuilds have different and usually much broader dates.

labels.de: Frühes 7. Jh. · Eine Halskette in Grab 90
labels.en: Early 7th century · A necklace in grave 90

summary.de: 625 steht für die erste Hälfte des siebten Jahrhunderts. In Grab 90 lagen im Brustbereich eine Fibel und Kettenperlen.
summary.en: 625 represents the first half of the seventh century. A brooch and necklace beads were found at chest level in grave 90.

labels.de: Spätes 7. Jh. · Gräber innerhalb des Hofzauns
labels.en: Late 7th century · Burials inside the farmyard fence

summary.de: 685 liegt im Datierungsfenster zweier Gräber, die der zweite Zaun umschloss. Sein Baujahr ist unbekannt.
summary.en: 685 falls within the dating range for two burials enclosed by the second fence. Its construction year is unknown.

summary.de: Der letzte Jahrring der frisch verarbeiteten Kammer-Eiche ergibt die Fällzeit Winter 703/704. Stork setzt die Beisetzung an den Jahresanfang 704. Das Fertigungsjahr des Betts bleibt offen.
summary.en: The outermost ring of the freshly worked chamber oak places its felling in the winter of 703/704. Stork dates the burial to early 704. The bed’s year of manufacture remains open.

summary.de: Ein Webgewicht, Perlen einer Halskette und ein ausgebessertes Bett erzählen vom Leben an der Jagst. In Mittelhofen lassen sich sogar die Zäune verfolgen, die manche Höfe nach und nach um ihre Gräber zogen.
summary.en: A loom weight, necklace beads and a repaired bed open up life on the Jagst. At Mittelhofen it is even possible to follow the changing fence lines as some farmyards began to enclose graves.
